newsitem.title: UK: SHELL OFF IN LONDON ON WEAKER CRUDE PRICE.
newsitem.headline: SHELL OFF IN LONDON ON WEAKER CRUDE PRICE.

text.p: Shares in oil majors British Petroleum and Shell Transport and Trading continued their recent run of weakness on Monday amid lower crUde oil prices and strengthening sterling.

BP was down 4-1/2p at 641-1/2p and Shell was off 6-1/2p to 973-1/2p by 1003 GMT. "The oil price is under pressure and sterling is another negative as the oils are very much dollar stocks," said Peter Hitchens, oil analyst at Williams de Broe.
Brent crude prices have lost ground over recent weeks, falling to around $22.50 a barrel after peaking at $25.06 a barrel in mid-October.
Meanwhile, sterling is benefiting from a tightening of monetary policy last week, rising to $1.6387/92 by 0735 GMT and with more gains seen likely.
"The oils still have perhaps another ten percent downside," Hitchens said. "I'd be holding at current levels but would become a buyer of BP around 6.0 stg."
Shell was also suffering from disappointing third quarter results, analysts said.
"The valuations of both Royal Dutch and Shell look stretched relative to those of their peers," said Salomon Brothers in their latest research. "We recommend investors take profits."
Elsewhere, analysts said weekend press speculation that Gulf, Elf, and Murco intend to merge their forecourt and refining operations was unlikely to impact much on the shares.
"If we do see a further rationalisation in the fuel retailing sector it will be positive for fuel retailers," Hitchens said. "But the net impact on the likes of BP and Shell will be negligible."
